chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the matter that a seeker seeks from his Lord, he said: 'Give charity during your day to sixty poor people; upon each poor person is one Sa' (measure), by the Sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So when he and his family). So when it is night, you bathe in the remaining third (of the night) and wear the least that one who has dependents wears from clothes, except that upon you, from those clothes, should be an izar (loincloth).

Then you pray two Rak'at. So when you place your forehead in the final Rak'at for prostration, you extol Allah, magnify Him, glorify Him, and sanctify Him, and mention your sins, and acknowledge with what you recognize from them specifically, then you raise your head.

Then when you place your head for the second prostration, you seek the choice of Allah one hundred times: 'O Allah, I seek Your choice.' Then you supplicate to Allah with whatever you wish, and ask Him of it; and every time you prostrate, expose your knees to the ground, then raise the loincloth so that you expose them, and place the loincloth behind you between your buttocks and the inner part of your shins.

key_terms.إِزَاراً: A loincloth or lower garment, specified here as a required item of clothing for the ritual.
key_terms.اسْتَخَرْتَ: To seek the best choice or divine preference from God.
key_terms.السُّجُودِ: Prostration, a key component of the prayer ritual described.
key_terms.رُكْبَتَيْكَ: The two knees, which are to be exposed to the ground during prostration in this specific ritual.
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A traditional unit of volume/measurement for charity, specifically the Sa' of the Prophet.

ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step ritual for performing the prayer to fulfill a specific need in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual of Salat al-Hajah, emphasizing the integration of material charity (sadaqah to sixty poor) with spiritual devotion to prepare the heart for supplication. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on specific physical postures, such as uncovering the knees during prostration, as acts of humility that facilitate the acceptance of one's requests from Allah.
